Deep ocean trenches form below, and volcanoes form above!

What happens as the plate sinks at the Philippine Trench?

It produces earthquakes! These are the earthquakes that PHIVOLCS carefully monitors.

How do volcanoes get their magma?

When a plate sinks, rock deep underground melts into magma that feeds the volcanoes above!
The Philippines has many volcanoes like Mayon and Taal! A sinking plate meets the mantle's heat, melting rock into magma that erupts.

How is the trench connected to our volcanoes?

As the plate sinks into Earth's hot interior, it melts into magma! This magma rises up to build volcanoes nearby.

Why doesn't the trench just fill up with mud and sand?

The plate keeps sinking! Even if sediment falls in, it stays deep because the ground is always moving down.

Along the eastern edge of the Philippines lies the Philippine Trench—a super deep crack in the sea floor where one plate slides under another. That same motion builds the earthquakes, volcanoes, and islands!

Why do the Philippine islands curve like a smile on the map?

They sit above a curved boundary where one plate dives under another. This curved row of volcanic islands is called an island arc!
When denser oceanic crust meets continental crust, it sinks because it's heavier. The melting crust creates magma that rises to form volcanoes!

How does the angle of a diving plate change where volcanoes pop up?

The angle at which a plate subducts affects the volcanic arc's position! A steeper subduction angle places the volcanic arc closer to the trench, shifting where volcanoes appear in the Philippine subduction system!

Why do Philippine island arc volcanoes form at a specific distance from the subduction trench?

The subducted plate must reach about 100 km deep to melt and make magma! This space is called the 'arc-trench gap'.
Oceanic crust is thinner but heavier, while continental crust is thicker but lighter. When they collide, the heavier oceanic crust sinks underneath!
The Philippine Trench is a deep oceanic trench formed by the subduction of the Philippine Sea plate!

How does a volcano erupt from deep underground?

Subducting oceanic crust melts into magma, rising through cracks in the continental plate to build pressure and erupt explosively as a volcano!

briefs.competency: make a simple electromagnet and observe and record its properties
existing_facts_en: Wind wire around an iron nail and add current to make an electromagnet! It’s a cool magnet you can easily switch on and off.
An electromagnet is a cool magnet made by electricity! It is only magnetic while electric current flows through it.
Placing a piece of iron inside the wire coil makes the electromagnet much, much stronger!

How can you make an electromagnet even stronger?

The stronger the electric current flowing, the stronger the electromagnet becomes!
An electromagnet has a north pole and a south pole, just like your ordinary magnet!
You can build a simple electromagnet by wrapping wire around a nail and connecting the ends to a battery!
You can make a magnet using electricity! Just wrap wire around iron to create a cool electromagnet.

How can you make an electromagnet stronger?

Put an iron nail in the middle of the coil! The iron boosts the magnetic force from the electricity, making it strong enough to pull more objects.
Want a stronger electromagnet? Add more wire loops to the coil, or use a more powerful battery! More loops and more current equal a stronger magnet.
Many think electromagnets pull every metal, but that's a mistake! They only pull iron and a few similar metals. They cannot pull gold, copper, or aluminum.

Can you build your own electromagnet at home?

Yes, it's easy! Wrap thin wire around an iron nail, connect the ends to a battery, and test how many paper clips it can pick up!

How can you test how strong your electromagnet is?

Count how many paper clips it can pick up! The more clips that stick, the stronger your electromagnet is.
Wrap a nail with wire and connect it to a battery! It becomes an electromagnet that can pull iron objects while current flows.
Running an electric current through a wire coiled around an iron nail temporarily magnetizes the nail to pick up paperclips.

Can a simple iron nail become a magnet?

Yes! Wrapping it with wire and passing an electric current aligns its magnetic domains, temporarily turning it into a magnet!

Want to make a super strong electromagnet with a nail?

Wrap 50 coils of wire around it! It creates a stronger electromagnet than just 10 coils.
An electromagnet wakes up when electric current flows through its coiled wire, creating a temporary magnetic field!

briefs.competency: use models or illustrations to explain how movements along faults generate earthquakes and identify and explain which types of faults are most likely to occur in the Philippines and explain why
existing_facts_en: As rocks on both sides of a fault slowly grind, stress builds up until it suddenly releases. That sudden slip causes an earthquake!
When tectonic plates suddenly slip or push against each other, their stored energy is released as a shaking earthquake!

What causes an earthquake underground?

A fault is a crack in large underground rocks! When these two sides suddenly slip, an earthquake happens.
An earthquake happens when huge rock blocks suddenly slip on opposite sides of a crack called a fault, making the ground shake!

How does an earthquake happen?

It happens when rocks on either side of a fault suddenly slip, releasing energy that shakes the ground!
The Philippine Fault is a 'strike-slip' fault! Two huge blocks of land slide sideways past each other, like rubbing hands. When they suddenly slip, an earthquake happens!
The Philippine Fault isn't just one line! It's made of connected 'segments' from Luzon to Mindanao. Sometimes, only one segment moves to cause an earthquake!

Does the Philippine Fault moving cause volcanoes to erupt?

Nope! This fault causes earthquakes because rocks shift, not because of magma or lava. Volcanic eruptions are a totally different thing with their own causes!

What is a fault?

A fault is a crack in Earth's surface where two sides of the ground can move. When they suddenly slip, the ground shakes — an earthquake! That's why we practice duck, cover, and hold — especially with the West Valley Fault near Metro Manila!

Why are earthquakes sudden if plates move so slowly?

Plates move just centimeters a year, as slow as fingernails grow! But pressure builds up bit by bit until it suddenly releases as a shaking earthquake!

How does the Philippine Fault Zone move?

This 1,200 km long strike-slip fault crosses the Philippines! It moves horizontally in a left-lateral sense: if you stand on it and look across, the far side moves left!
The Marikina Valley Fault System in Luzon is a right-lateral strike-slip fault!
Tectonic plates suddenly slip past each other along a fault line, releasing years of stored stress as shaking seismic waves!
Sudden slipping along a fault line releases stored elastic energy in rocks, generating seismic waves that shake the ground.
Tectonic plates slowly push until stress overcomes friction, making rocks snap and release earthquake waves!
The Valley Fault System in Luzon is a huge geological fracture. This is where massive tectonic plates slowly grind past each other!
Tectonic plates sticking together build up stress until the rock fractures, releasing energy as powerful seismic earthquake waves!

briefs.competency: collaborate in a class discussion to recognize the advantages and limitations of using series or parallel circuits
existing_facts_en: A series circuit has only one path for current! If just one part breaks, all the lights go out together.
A parallel circuit has many separate paths for current. Even if one light goes out, the others keep shining bright!

What happens if one bulb burns out in a series circuit?

Everything stops! In a series circuit, parts share a single path. If one bulb burns out, the whole circuit stops and all lights go off.

Why do other bulbs stay lit if one goes out in a parallel circuit?

Because each bulb has its own branch! In a parallel circuit, they don't share a single path, so the others stay lit even if one goes out.
In a parallel circuit, the path branches and current splits into separate routes. This is home wiring! Turn off one light, others keep working because each has its own path.
In a parallel circuit, each branch receives the full battery voltage — this is why lights in a parallel circuit shine brighter than those in a series circuit with the same battery.
In a series circuit, if one bulb breaks, all bulbs go out because the single path for current is interrupted — this is why old-style Christmas string lights all went dark if one bulb failed.
Philippine homes use parallel circuits! This means turning off the living room light won't affect the kitchen, and every outlet gets 220 volts.

Why do two bulbs glow dimly when placed in series with one battery?

Both glow dimly because the added resistance reduces the current flowing through each bulb!

Why did old Christmas lights all go out if just one bulb burned out?

Because they were wired in series! If one small bulb burned out, the whole circuit broke and all the other lights went out too.

What's the big difference between series and parallel circuits?

In a series circuit, if one component fails, they all fail. In parallel (like house lights), the others stay on even if one fails.
Adding more bulbs in series to the same battery makes them all dimmer! This happens because total resistance increases, which reduces the current flowing through each bulb.
In a parallel circuit, each branch works independently! If one bulb or appliance fails, the rest keep working normally.

Why do all the parol lights go dark if just one bulb burns out?

Because they are wired in series! The current flows through a single path, so one broken bulb breaks the whole circuit.

Why do all the lights go out when one bulb breaks in a series circuit?

A single burned-out bulb breaks the entire path! This turns off all the other lights in the string.
In a parallel circuit, each branch receives the full battery voltage! The bulbs stay bright even when more of them are added.

Why are houses wired in parallel circuits?

Houses are wired in parallel circuits so each light and appliance can be switched on or off separately without affecting the others!

briefs.competency: describe mutations as changes in DNA or chromosomes and discuss some of the factors that cause mutations, such as infectious agents, radiation, and chemicals
existing_facts_en: An insertion mutation adds one or more nucleotide bases into the DNA sequence, which can shift the reading frame and change many amino acids.
Mutations can alter a protein's structure and function, because changing the amino acid sequence can change how the protein folds and what job it can do.
Sunburn happens when UV rays from the sun damage the DNA in your skin cells; getting sunburned again and again raises your risk of skin cancer later on.

What causes Down syndrome?

Having three copies of chromosome 21 instead of two — this happens when chromosomes fail to separate properly during meiosis, called nondisjunction.

What is a mutation?

A mutation is a change in DNA — it might do nothing, help, or hurt the living thing that has it!

What makes DNA mutate?

DNA can change from a copying mistake, or from too much sunlight (UV), cigarette smoke, or certain chemicals — that's why sun protection matters!

What causes mutations in DNA?

Things like radiation and certain chemicals, or copying mistakes in DNA — and if it happens in sex cells, it can pass to the next generation.

What is a silent mutation?

Not all mutations show. In a silent mutation, a DNA letter changes but the protein stays the same — like a typo you can still read as the same word.

What happens when DNA makes a copying mistake?

Sometimes when DNA copies itself, a base gets swapped by mistake — this is called a mutation, like a typo in writing. Some have no effect; others cause changes.

What is a mutation?

A mutation is a change in the DNA sequence — a part might be altered, deleted, or added, and this can change how a gene works.

Mutation and variation aren't the same. Variation is differences we already inherit, like eye color or height. A mutation is a brand-new DNA change happening now — and it's actually where all variation first came from.

How can one tiny gene change cause disease?

Genes use DNA to build proteins, the tiny machines that run your body. Change a letter in a gene, and the protein's shape can go wrong — that's how some mutations cause disease.

What causes DNA mutations?

UV light, radiation, certain chemicals, or even random copying errors when DNA duplicates itself can all cause mutations.
Mutations are changes in DNA, and they create new variation that can be passed down to offspring.

What is a mutation?

It's a change in the DNA code — sometimes it does nothing, but sometimes it creates a brand-new trait.

What causes mutations in DNA?

Mutations can be caused by things like radiation and certain chemicals that damage DNA.

How does space travel affect an astronaut's body?

Cosmic radiation from stars can damage the DNA inside white blood cells, temporarily weakening an astronaut's immune system!

briefs.competency: describe a valence electron as an electron in the outer shell of an atom that can take part in formation of bonds
existing_facts_en: Chlorine has the electron configuration 1s2 2s2 2p6 3s2 3p5, with seven valence electrons, placing it in group 17 of the periodic table.
Carbon has the electron configuration 1s2 2s2 2p2, with four valence electrons, placing it in group 14 of the periodic table.
The outer electrons of atoms act like glue, joining them together to form substances!
Atoms join together to fill their outer electron shell, because a full shell makes them more stable!
Noble gases like helium, neon, and argon almost never bond! Their outer shell is already full, so they don't need to gain or share electrons.
In a covalent bond, the shared pair of electrons counts for both atoms! This makes each atom's outer shell seem full.

How many bonds can an atom form?

The number of valence electrons decides! For example, carbon has four valence electrons, so it forms exactly four bonds.

What's really happening inside a metal that lets it carry electricity?

In a metal, atoms share their outer electrons in something like a sea of free electrons!
Atoms give away electrons to be stable! This means having a FULL outer shell of 8 electrons. Giving or taking electrons helps them reach this stable state.
A Lewis dot structure is a cool diagram using dots to show an atom's valence electrons and how they share to form chemical bonds!

Why don't noble gases react with other elements?

Helium, neon, and argon have full outermost electron shells! Since they're already stable, they don't need to form bonds with anything.
Noble gases are completely unreactive because their outer electron shell is already totally full!
Valence electrons are the electrons in an atom's outermost shell! They are the boss that decides how the atom will bond with other atoms.

What are valence electrons?

They are the electrons in the outermost shell! They mainly determine how an atom bonds or reacts with other atoms.

How do atoms bond and connect with each other?

They share or transfer their outer electrons, not their nuclei! It is the electrons that make all the chemical connections!

Where are valence electrons found, and what do they do?

They are in the outermost shell! They decide how the atom will bond with other atoms.
Atoms bond to one another by transferring or sharing their outer electrons to stick together!

briefs.competency: explain how increased societal uses of renewable energies could mitigate the effects of global climate change, including how the Philippines could make better use of its plentiful natural resources
existing_facts_en: To cut carbon dioxide, we use smoke-free solar and wind energy! The Philippines gets tons of sunshine, making it a perfect source of clean electricity that doesn't add to greenhouse gases.

How does renewable energy help fight climate change?

By using renewable energy, we burn fewer fossil fuels! This means less carbon dioxide is released — the gas that warms our Earth and causes climate change.
Clean energy like solar and wind power makes no carbon dioxide, so it helps fight climate change!
Renewable energy is much cleaner! It does not release smoke or pollution while making electricity, unlike burning coal or oil.
Geothermal energy is renewable because the Earth's heat never runs out—it's always there! It's also cleaner than coal since it releases much less smoke into the air.

Why is geothermal cleaner than a coal plant?

Coal plants burn fuel that runs out and makes lots of smoke! Geothermal burns nothing, just using Earth's heat, so it’s cleaner.
Wave energy is renewable — wind keeps making waves, and it creates no smoke or pollution like burning coal or oil!
The Philippines has huge wind energy potential! Especially in Ilocos Norte, the northern tip of Luzon, and parts of Mindanao — where winds are strong and reliable.
To slow Earth's warming, we must cut greenhouse gas emissions! We can do this by using clean energy like solar and wind, saving electricity, and planting trees.
Using clean energy from the sun, wind, and water helps cut down the carbon dioxide that warms our Earth!
Using clean energy like solar and wind power releases fewer greenhouse gases!
We can lower carbon dioxide in the air! Just plant trees, use clean energy like solar power, and save electricity and fuel every day.
We can reduce greenhouse gases by using clean energy like solar panels, windmills, and hydropower! Since they don't burn fossil fuels, they make electricity without releasing carbon dioxide.

How is the Philippines achieving a cleaner future?

By expanding renewable energy like solar, wind, geothermal, and hydroelectric to reduce greenhouse gas emissions!

How does the Philippines use its volcanoes to create clean energy?

The Tongonan geothermal field in Leyte supplies a large share of the Visayas' electricity! It shows how the Philippines' volcanic nature can be used for clean and renewable energy.
Enhanced Geothermal Systems (EGS) unlock hot underground rock even without natural water! Engineers drill deep, pump water down, and capture the steam to expand geothermal energy potential.
Geothermal energy releases far less carbon dioxide than coal plants! While coal causes air pollution and climate change with its emissions, geothermal uses Earth's renewable heat with minimal impact.

What renewable energy is the Philippines focusing on?

The Philippines is strengthening geothermal (its largest renewable source), solar, and wind energy to reduce reliance on imported coal and lower carbon emissions.

briefs.competency: discuss the factors that limit the ecosystem's carrying capacity, such as adequate food, shelter, water, and mates
existing_facts_en: Population growth influences the carrying capacity of an ecosystem — the maximum number of individuals an environment can support.

Why can't a few animals just grow into a huge population instantly?

Because mates are a limiting factor; if there are not enough partners to reproduce, the population cannot grow quickly.
Predators help keep the number of their prey close to what the environment can support — the carrying capacity.
Carrying capacity isn't fixed — it rises in the rainy season when food is plentiful, and drops during a drought.
When animals live too crowded together, disease spreads faster and their numbers start to drop.

What stops animal populations from growing too big?

Limiting factors like food scarcity, disease, and predators control how big animal populations get and keep them from growing too large.
Because deserts have so few plants, only a small number of animals can survive there too.
How much food a place has limits how many animals can actually live there!
Too many fish crammed in one pond means the oxygen runs low, and that makes them easy to get sick.
A bigger habitat with plenty of food can support more animals — it has a higher carrying capacity than a small place.

Why does the tamaraw population grow so slowly?

Because tamaraws live alone and have trouble meeting up to breed, their population grows even more slowly — which is why protecting every single one matters.
When forests in Mindoro disappear, the carrying capacity for the tamaraw drops, leaving very few of them behind.
When too many grass-eating animals crowd one place, the plants get used up fast — and the land itself gets damaged.
The size of a population is held in check by factors like food and water shortage, disease, competition, and predators.
When a population grows past what its environment can support, resources run short and its numbers can suddenly drop from hunger or disease.
Carrying capacity isn't one fixed number, it changes depending on the food, weather, and condition of a place.

Is carrying capacity the same for every animal?

No! Each kind of animal has its own carrying capacity because they need different amounts of food and space.

What is 'carrying capacity'?

It's the biggest number of a certain organism an environment can support without running out of food, water, and space.

briefs.competency: describe different science process skills used in performing simple science activities, such as observing, predicting, and measuring using units such as millimeter, centimeter, and meter
existing_facts_en: The Philippine Eagle can grow to almost 1 meter — about 100 centimeters — from its head all the way to its tail!
Before we measure, we can first estimate or guess how big or heavy an object might be!

How do you get an accurate reading from a thermometer?

Look at the thermometer at the exact same level as your eye!
The meter is the perfect unit for measuring length or distance! We use it every day.
For measuring how long things are, the meter (m) is the SI base unit of length.

How do we measure the length of things?

We use a ruler to measure length in centimeters or meters!

How do we measure exactly how long things are?

We use a meter stick! It is one meter long and marked every centimeter to measure length.
A ruler is a handy tool for measuring length! It has centimeter and millimeter marks to show exactly how long an object is.
A ruler is a tool for measuring length! It usually has centimeter and millimeter marks so your measurement is always exact.
A tape measure is a flexible tool marked in units like centimeters and meters to measure the length of things!
A ruler is a straight tool with centimeter and millimeter marks — perfect for measuring how long something is!

Did you know each centimeter on a ruler hides smaller parts?

Yes! Each centimeter is divided into ten millimeters, so you can measure tiny lengths super accurately!
A rain gauge is a tool that catches and measures how much rain falls in millimeters, telling us exactly how heavy the rain was!

How do scientists measure how much rain fell?

They use a rain gauge — a container left outside to catch rain! Scientists measure how high the water rose inside it in millimeters. More millimeters means heavier rain fell.
A rain gauge is like a marked cup that catches rain! Water collects inside, and we read how many millimeters high it reaches. That tells us how much rain fell!

How do we measure rainfall?

We use a rain gauge! It's a simple container that measures rain in millimeters. Just read the water level after it rains!

What tool measures how much rain has fallen?

A rain gauge is a container with a scale that tells the amount of rainwater in millimeters!
To find out how much it rained, we catch rainwater in a container and measure the depth of the collected water, usually in millimeters!

briefs.competency: describe the changes in the direction and length of shadows from a shadow stick and use the information to infer why the Sun changes position during a day
existing_facts_en:
Why do shadows change size during the day?

As the sun moves! It's longer in the morning and afternoon, but shorter at noon.
In the morning, the shadow points west because the sun is in the east; a shadow always points away from the light.
In the Philippines, your shadow is shortest around noon because the sun is almost directly overhead!

Ever wonder why your shadow changes size during the day?

The length of a shadow changes depending on the angle at which the light hits the object! Cool, right?
When the sun sits low in the sky, your shadow stretches out super long! But when the sun is high overhead, your shadow becomes short and stubby.
A sundial tells time using the shadow of an upright piece called a gnomon — as the Sun moves across the sky, the shadow moves across the numbered markings.
Your shadow is longest in the early morning because the low angle of the Sun blocks light across a greater distance!
The shadow of a coconut tree is shortest at exactly noon when the sun is directly overhead!
Shadows change length and direction because Earth's spin changes the Sun's position! They're long when the Sun is low, and short at noon when it's high.
In the morning, the shadow points west because the Sun is in the east. As the Sun moves west, the shadow slowly swings toward the east!

Can you build your own sun-clock?

Yes! Just stick an upright stick in the ground. Mark where the shadow tip lands each hour to make your own sundial!
At noon, the Sun is highest, making your shadow the shortest! At sunrise and sunset, the Sun is low, so shadows are longest.
Mark the shadow's tip all day—it traces a curved line, not straight! The Sun is high at noon and low in the morning and afternoon.
Our shadow changes length and direction all day! It is long in the morning and afternoon when the Sun is low, and shortest at noon when the Sun is high.

Why do shadows change?

Shadows change length and direction as the Sun moves across the sky! They are shortest at noon when the Sun is at its highest.
Plant a stick in the ground for a sundial! As the Sun moves across the sky, the stick's shadow shifts and changes length, showing time passing.
At noon in the Philippines, shadows point north because the Sun is directly overhead or slightly to the south!
A vertical stick casts its shortest shadow exactly at solar noon! This happens when the Sun reaches its highest point in the sky.

briefs.competency: gather information from secondary sources to identify and describe examples of innovative devices that can be used to transform heat energy into electrical energy
existing_facts_en:
Can we get electricity from a volcano without it erupting?

Yes! In geothermal power, we drill near a volcano's hot rock and use its heat to boil water into steam — making electricity safely!
Geothermal energy is heat from deep inside the earth! It boils water to make steam that spins a turbine and creates electricity.
In a geothermal plant, heat from deep inside the earth makes steam that spins a turbine to create power—just like at Tiwi and Makiling-Banahaw (Mak-Ban)!

Where does geothermal energy come from?

It comes from heat deep inside the Earth, which boils water into steam that spins a turbine!

How does heat turn into electricity inside the plant?

Heat (thermal energy) turns water into steam! The steam spins the turbine (motion), and that motion becomes electricity.

Can the ocean's temperature help make electricity?

Yes! OTEC (Ocean Thermal Energy Conversion) uses the temperature difference between warm surface water and cold deep water to generate electricity. The Philippines' tropical seas have huge potential for this!
The Tiwi Geothermal Power Plant in Albay converts underground thermal heat energy into electrical energy to power homes across the Luzon grid!
The Mak-Ban geothermal power plant in Laguna converts underground volcanic heat into electrical energy to power Luzon homes!
The Tiwi Power Plant in Albay converts thermal energy from underground volcanic steam into usable electricity!
The Tiwi Geothermal Power Plant in Albay taps into the extreme heat beneath Mount Malinao to harness thermal energy and make electricity!

How does the Malitbog Geothermal Power Plant make electricity?

The Malitbog Geothermal Power Plant in Leyte converts thermal energy from underground heat into electrical energy for the grid!
The Maibarara Geothermal Power Plant in Batangas converts thermal energy from underground hot water into electrical energy to power local homes!

How does a geothermal power plant make electricity?

Hot water and steam rise from deep underground! The steam spins a turbine connected to a generator, and that creates electricity for our homes.

How do we use Earth's internal heat?

That heat, linked to mantle convection, powers geothermal power plants to make electricity! The Philippines is one of the world's top users of geothermal energy.
The heat under active volcanoes can make electricity! This is called geothermal energy, and the Philippines has plants that use this underground heat for power.
The BacMan geothermal power plant in Sorsogon and Albay is one of the Philippines' biggest! It uses hot steam from volcanic ground near Mayon to make electricity.

How does hot steam from underground create electricity?

Hot steam from the ground rushes up through drilled wells and spins turbine blades! The spinning blades turn a generator that produces electricity.

Binary cycle geothermal plants heat a secondary fluid like isobutane using lower-temperature geothermal fluid! The isobutane boils easily and spins the turbine, even when the geothermal fluid isn't hot enough for direct flash steam.

briefs.competency: recognize that power is the rate of doing work
existing_facts_en: Power can also be calculated as P equals F times v times cosine theta, where F is force, v is velocity, and theta is the angle between them.

How is power measured?

Power is measured in watts (W)! One watt equals one joule of energy used or produced every single second.

How do we find power?

Power equals the work done divided by the time taken! If two machines do the same work, the faster one has greater power.
If two people climb the same stairs, they do the same work. But the one who runs has greater power — same work in less time!
Power shows how fast work is done! It is calculated by dividing the work by the time taken.
We measure power in watts! One watt simply means one joule of energy is used every second.
The watt rating on an appliance like an iron tells you exactly how much energy it uses each second!
Running up the stairs needs more power than walking! The work is the same, but running is faster.
Power is how fast energy is used or produced, measured in watts! Higher wattage means the work gets done faster.
If you do the exact same work in a shorter time, you need more power! Speeding up takes extra power.
Power is how fast work gets done! It equals work divided by time — measured in watts (one watt = one joule per second).
The 'watt' measures power, and this cool unit is named after the inventor James Watt!
The unit of power is the watt! It is named after the great inventor James Watt.

How do we measure power?

The watt is the unit that measures power! It shows how fast energy is used.

What is the formula for power?

Power equals work divided by time! The equation is Power = Work ÷ Time (P = W ÷ t).

How many joules are in one watt?

One watt equals one joule of energy per second! That means 1 W = 1 joule/second.

How much energy does a standard AA battery hold?

A standard AA battery stores 10,800 joules — enough to power a 1-watt LED for three hours, but a 10-watt bulb drains it in just 18 minutes!
A device with a higher watt rating uses more energy each second, so your electricity use adds up faster!

briefs.competency: calculate the number of protons, neutrons, and electrons in the atom of several elements, such as aluminum
existing_facts_en: A boron atom with mass number 11 and atomic number 5 has 5 protons, 5 electrons, and 6 neutrons.
The atomic number of helium (He) is 2, so it has exactly 2 protons!
The atomic number of lithium (Li) is 3, so it has exactly 3 protons!
The atomic number of carbon (C) is 6, so it has exactly 6 protons!
Did you know nitrogen (N) has an atomic number of 7? That means every nitrogen atom is packed with exactly 7 protons!
Oxygen (O) has an atomic number of 8! Because of this, every single oxygen atom contains exactly 8 protons.

How many protons does neon (Ne) have?

Neon (Ne) has an atomic number of 10, which means it has exactly 10 protons!
Sodium (Na) has an atomic number of 11! That means every sodium atom is packed with 11 protons.

What is the atomic number of magnesium (Mg)?

Magnesium (Mg) has an atomic number of 12, meaning it has exactly 12 protons!
Aluminum (Al) has an atomic number of 13. Because of this, it contains exactly 13 protons!
Silicon (Si) has an atomic number of 14! This means every silicon atom is made of 14 protons.
The atomic number of phosphorus (P) is 15, which means it has exactly 15 protons!

How many protons are inside sulfur (S)?

Its atomic number is 16, so sulfur (S) has exactly 16 protons!

What is the atomic number of chlorine (Cl)?

It's 17! The atomic number of chlorine (Cl) is 17, meaning it has 17 protons.

How many protons make up potassium (K)?

The atomic number of potassium (K) is 19, so it has exactly 19 protons!
Zinc (Zn) has an atomic number of 30, which means every zinc atom has exactly 30 protons!
Mercury (Hg) has an atomic number of 80, which means every mercury atom is made of 80 protons!
To find the number of neutrons, subtract the atomic number from the mass number! For example, 12 minus 6 gives us 6 neutrons in carbon.

briefs.competency: discuss the patterns of volcanic eruptions in the Philippines over the last 100 years with family and community members to assess and describe how predictable patterns of eruptions are
existing_facts_en: Mayon Volcano has erupted many times in the last hundred years! Nearby families often remember more than one big eruption.
In the Philippines, some volcanoes erupt often while others stay quiet for decades. The pattern is not the same for every mountain!
Taal Volcano erupted in 1965 and again in 2020! This shows a volcano can rest for decades and then wake quite suddenly.
PHIVOLCS writes down each eruption! This helps scientists and communities compare today's unrest with patterns from the last hundred years.

What is Kanlaon's eruption pattern?

Kanlaon on Negros has sent up ash and steam several times in recent decades. It's a pattern of restless but often smaller events!

How do towns near Bulusan handle its eruptions?

Bulusan in Sorsogon wakes with ash explosions now and then! Nearby towns treat this unrest as a repeating risk.

Why do communities near Taal watch for steaming and small quakes?

Because these exact signs happened right before several of Taal's modern eruptions! Watching them helps keep everyone safe.
Mayon often sends lava slowly down its slopes! This steady pattern gives nearby towns more time to prepare compared to a sudden, fast explosion.
Talking with elders about past eruptions is super helpful! It helps families learn if their volcano wakes up often or only after a very long rest.

Do Philippine volcanoes always erupt at the same time?

Nope! Some years, several show unrest close together, while other years stay quieter, making activity come in uneven clusters.

How do hazard maps help families stay safe?

Hazard maps from past eruptions show which rivers and slopes were hit before! This helps families talk about where danger tends to return.
Family stories about past eruptions plus PHIVOLCS records together show if a nearby volcano tends to wake up often or rarely!
Mayon showed strong unrest in 2018 with lava and ash! This is just one more event in its long pattern of waking many times.
PHIVOLCS keeps a permanent danger zone around some active volcanoes because past eruptions kept hitting the same close slopes!
Did you know PHIVOLCS counts steam-driven explosions as eruptions too? This means their pattern includes small events, not just famous giant blasts!
A volcano with no eruption this year can still be active! The last hundred years show long rests between the biggest events.

Why compare Mayon and Pinatubo?

Comparing Mayon's many eruptions with Pinatubo's rare giant blast helps families see that nearby volcanoes can follow very different clocks!

How do old deposit maps help people today?

Fast hot flows follow the same valleys used in earlier eruptions! So, old deposit maps still help people guess the next paths.
Talking about past eruptions with family and neighbors helps your class see volcano patterns, even if no volcano follows a perfect timetable!
